question: Each notch on a dial adds pain too small to feel and pays $10,000; the last notch is agony. Where should he stop?
options: At the notch where pain first shows
Wherever a plan made in advance says
answer: Wherever a plan made in advance says. In Warren Quinn's puzzle, each step brings money and no felt change, so step-by-step reasoning always says one more, and ends in agony. Quinn argued he must pick a stopping point beforehand and keep to it. Snacks, scrolling and overtime are all one more imperceptible notch.
move: Decide the stopping point before the steps, because no single step will tell you.
ask: Which habit am I letting grow one harmless-looking step at a time?
trap: Where pain first shows, though no single notch ever shows it.
reference: Quinn, The Puzzle of the Self-Torturer, Philosophical Studies 59 (1), 1990
